headline: Set November 30 deadline for alcohol license renewals; approved one-day alcohol license for Claddagh Pub cornhole tournament.
summary: An outdoor cornhole fundraiser for the Hibernians will serve beer, and all city departments signed off on the license. Officials also discussed late alcohol renewal applications, and the clerk will check whether a $100 late fee is possible.
decisions: Approved a One-Day All Alcohol license for the Claddagh Pub's September 19, 2026 cornhole tournament, with all members in favor.
Set November 30 as the deadline for alcohol license renewal applications.

Chairman Chase stated that all alcohol renewal applicants should have their renewals in the system going forward by November 30th as a deadline.

MEETING MINUTES 
 
METHUEN LICENSING BOARD 
SEARLES BUILDING, 41 PLEASANT STREET 
SECOND FLOOR CONFERENCE ROOM #208  
 
Chairman Chase called the meeting to order.  
 
Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
Meeting of the Methuen Licensing Board on September 9, 2026, 41 Pleasant Street called to order by Chairman 
Chase. Members present were Chairman Chase, Commissioner Fisher and Commissioner Camargo.  
 
Approval of the agenda for September 9, 2026. Commissioner Fisher motioned to approve the agenda for July 
8, 2026. Commissioner Camargo seconded. All in favor. 
  
Approval of minutes from July 8, 2026, licensing meeting. Commissioner Camargo motioned to approve the 
minutes from July 8, 2026, licensing meeting. Commissioner Fisher seconded. All in favor.  
 
NEW BUSINESS 
 
An application has been submitted from the Claddagh Pub and Restaurant, 171 Pelham St, for a One-
Day All Alcohol license for their annual cornhole tournament to be held on Saturday, September 19, 
2026, from 12:00 pm – 5:00 pm. 
 
Brian Farrell, 171 Pelham Street, Methuen is present to speak to the event.  Local Hibernian group has 
been doing a cornhole tournament at the Claddagh – an outdoor fundraiser for the Hibernians.  He says 
they’ve had this even for the past 6 years or so. 
 
Chairman Chase asked if there was going to be a mobile bar setup. Mr. Farrell stated it will be one 
bartender with a cooler, basically serving beers. Chairman Chase asked if patrons would be allowed to 
walk from the outdoor area back into the Claddagh. Mr. Farrell stated that they are allowed to do so but 
the alcohol has to stay outside. So, they would go in for the restrooms or to order food. Chairman Chase
The City of Methuen is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer in its Programs and Activities  
asked if it was a full bar or just beer. Mr. Farrell stated that last year he set up the bar and it was pretty 
much all just beer and that they have all the mixed drinks in cans. Chairman Chase asked who Arthur 
Hoffman is. Mr. Farrell stated he is one of the bartenders and has been there for many years. All 
departments from the city signed off on the one-day alcohol license.  
 
Commissioner Fisher motioned to approve the application submitted from the Claddagh Pub and 
Restaurant, 171 Pelham St, for a One-Day All Alcohol license for their annual cornhole tournament to 
be held on Saturday, September 19, 2026, from 12:00 pm – 5:00 pm, Commissioner Camargo seconded, 
all in favor. 
 
Next meeting is October 14th and Commissioner Camargo stated she will not be available for that meeting. 
Commissioner Fisher and Chairman Chase stated they will be there. 
 
Chairman Chase wished to discuss the end of year alcohol and auto licensing coming up. It was stated that some 
applicants do not get their applications in on time and there are presently no repercussions for this. The 
discussion was surrounding the deadline for application for alcohol license renewals, specifically, and how to 
handle very late applicants. 
 
The clerk stated that the process kicks off about the 1st of November and that it continues on a rolling basis 
through end of year. Very late applications are not ideal as this leaves all the sign-off departments with very 
little time for proper inspections of establishments. The clerk stated that her time is often spent emailing, phone 
calling and otherwise trying to prompt applicants to do their renewals especially as it gets later in the year 
(beyond November 30th).  
 
Chairman Chase stated that all alcohol renewal applicants should have their renewals in the system going 
forward by November 30th as a deadline.  He asked that we discuss with the Solicitor’s office if a $100 late fee 
is possible for applicants filing after November 30th. The clerk will follow up on this and report back.  
 
Chairman Chase made a motion to adjourn. All in favor.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Next meeting will be October 14, 2026. 
 
Respectfully Submitted by 
Beth Rizzo 
Licensing Clerk
